name: Fluid Checks & Top-Offs
summary: Second pass found BMW owner's manual text (MY2011 E90, E94 and 328i xDrive editions on third-party hosts; the 2010 edition could not be read) that now PRIMARY-verifies: the electronic oil-level check (iDrive path, stalk buttons, warm-engine drive condition, 1 US qt / 125 mile rule), coolant is half water and half BMW-approved additive and must be checked cold with the cap opened in two stages and the level between MAX and MIN marks in the filler neck, and the window washer system (including headlamp washers) holds about 6.3 US qt / 6.0 L. Brake fluid is DOT 4 with a 2-year change interval from E9x-specific secondary sources (E92 M3, BMW part listings) and a BMW E46 handbook; no E9x brake-fluid manual page was reachable, so it is VERIFIED_SECONDARY, not VERIFIED. Closed: brake reservoir is under the plastic cover at the driver-side base of the windshield (the cabin microfilter housing cover on E9x); power steering on the N52 E90 328i appears hydraulic (ECS/Turner catalogs list a reservoir and CHF 11S fluid; a 2008 E90 328i owner replaced the pump); BMW coolant 82141467704 confirmed by two retailers. Still open: E90 328i coolant capacity (only other-model figures of about 8.2-8.5 L), washer-fluid spec and exact filler location (single source), expansion tank location (single source), brake-reservoir cover fastener count, automatic transmission and differential fluid specs, and the whole power-steering fluid check procedure (not an owner item in the manual's engine-compartment list). Build as 'check levels and top off' only.
variantDependencies: Engine: oil-level method is electronic on N52; the MY2011 E90 manual also describes a dipstick method (likely for diesel) so confirm the car has no dipstick. N51 (SULEV) not separately researched.
Transmission: manual vs automatic changes coolant capacity per unsourced Z4 forum figures (8.2 L MT / 8.5 L AT) and transmission fluid; no E90 328i figure found. Auto fluid spec MISSING.
Drive: xDrive adds transfer case and front differential fluids; not researched in any source.

Steering: ECS lists hydraulic reservoirs for E90 328i N52 split by 'with/without active steering'; forum posts say Efficient Dynamics cars from 09/2007 had EPS. A 2010 328i with active steering has a different reservoir (32416767161 vs 32416851218). Inspect the car.
Model year / build: cabin filter housing cover procedure per Bentley applies to cars built up to 12/2007; a 2010 car may differ, which also affects brake-reservoir access.
Headlamp washers: the 6.3 qt washer capacity includes headlamp washers; a car without them may differ.

tools.item: Funnel, clean rags, clean syringe or baster
tools.note: Generic; one source mentions a syringe to remove overfilled brake fluid.

tools.item: 8 mm socket and ratchet (to lift the cowl microfilter housing cover for brake reservoir access)
tools.note: bmwblog is an E92 M3; bavmods covers E90-E93 (four 8 mm screws); bimmerpost is a 2006 330i (six). Count conflict is in guide 10.

tools.item: Distilled water for the 50/50 coolant mix
tools.note: BMW manual says 'half water and half additive' without naming distilled water; three secondary sources use distilled/de-ionised water.

parts.note: Turner lists E90 328i N52 and calls it BMW coolant, nitrite/phosphate-free, 50/50 with distilled water, 8+ L systems. Bimmerworld notes BMW changed formula for 2018+ cars. A second Turner listing (Febi 1.5 L, same number cross-referenced) calls it 'G11' while a forum and Bimmerworld call BMW blue 'G48' type: naming differs, so buy the BMW-branded 82141467704 and do not mix coolant types.

parts.item: DOT 4 brake fluid (Genuine BMW 1 gal / 12 fl oz; ATE Typ 200 BF1200 DOT 4 listed for 328i)
parts.note: FCP lists the Genuine BMW DOT 4 numbers (not E90-specific fitment) and ATE Typ 200 for the 328i. The youcanic article independently names ATE Type 200 as the alternative and says DOT 4 is the most common BMW fluid; a bimmerpost thread also recommends ATE Typ 200 (amber). Use any fresh sealed DOT 4.

parts.item: Washer fluid (any automotive washer fluid; spec not found)
parts.note: No BMW fluid spec or additive restriction found in retrievable manual pages.

parts.item: Power steering fluid CHF 11S (reference only; not an owner top-up item in the manual)
parts.note: ECS lists Genuine BMW CHF 11S for the E90 328i N52; Turner's E9x service kit includes CHF 11S. Neither names which E90 cars use it; hydraulic reservoir 32416851218 'without active steering' vs 32416767161 'with active steering' per ECS.

fluids.spec: Electronic readout. Engine must be at operating temperature after at least about 6.2 miles (10 km) of uninterrupted driving. Instrument cluster: press button 1 on the turn-indicator lever up/down until the OIL symbol appears, then press button 2 (check takes about 3 minutes stationary, about 5 minutes driving). iDrive: Vehicle Info > Vehicle status > Engine oil level. Add up to 1 US quart / 1 L only after the display asks, and within 125 miles. 'Level too high': have it checked.
fluids.conflicts: The E90 manual also documents a dipstick check (probably diesel cars); other sources say the N52 has none.

fluids.spec: Half water, half BMW-approved additive (blue BMW coolant). Use only additives suitable for BMW; do not add coolant when hot; do not mix coolant types. Check with the engine cold: turn the expansion tank cap slightly counterclockwise to relieve pressure, then open fully; level correct between MAX and MIN marks in the filler neck; close the cap until it clicks audibly; have repeated loss investigated.
fluids.capacity: E90 328i capacity NOT found. Other-model reports: 8.2 L MT / 8.5 L AT (E89 Z4 forum, unsourced), 8.4 L (N55 AT, Bentley quoted on a forum), 'about 8 L' (E90 335d forum), '8+ L' (Turner). Top-offs do not need the figure.
fluids.conflicts: Spec/procedure VERIFIED from two BMW manuals plus retailers. Capacity: MISSING for this car (capacity line status MISSING).

fluids.spec: DOT 4; change about every 2 years (BMW recommendation reported; CBS tracks it); do not mix DOT 3 into DOT 4; never use fluid from an open container; fill only to just below MAX; brake fluid damages paint.
fluids.conflicts: The only BMW document naming DOT 4 and the 2-year interval is a 2003/04 3 Series (E46) handbook, a different chassis. The MY2011 E90 manual lists brake fluid only as a Condition Based Service item (p.231) and warns it harms paint. Gearshifters also quotes 30,000 mi (reader comment). Another forum says 'annual flush' as opinion.

fluids.spec: Filler neck serves both the window washers and the headlamp washers (BMW manual); no BMW fluid spec found
fluids.capacity: about 6.3 US qt / 6.0 L including headlamp washers
fluids.note: Capacity appears in two BMW manuals (sedan 2011 p.258, coupe/convertible 2011 p.250) but on the same host.

fluids.spec: CHF 11S (BMW 83290429576 / Pentosin CHF11S) reported by two parts catalogs for the E90 328i N52; manual does not list the reservoir among owner-serviced engine compartment items
fluids.status: VERIFIED_SECONDARY (type: hydraulic reservoir listed for the car); capacity MISSING
fluids.conflicts: Forum posts say some 2007-09+ cars have EPS (no fluid); a 2008 E90 328i 6MT owner replaced the belt-driven pump and bled the system (hydraulic). Which a given VIN has is unresolved.

fluids.spec: author used Royal Purple Synchromax; no OE spec given

fluids.item: Automatic transmission / differential / transfer case fluid

torque.value: No torque; BMW manual says turn until it clicks audibly
torque.conflicts: A bimmerpost thread reports a coolant leak when the cap was not fully seated.

steps.title: Prep
steps.instruction: Park on level ground with the engine off. Before opening the hood make sure the wiper arms rest against the windshield (BMW manual). For coolant the engine must be fully cold; wait at least 30-60 minutes after driving.
warnings: Do not open the hood while the engine is hot and never open the coolant cap on a hot engine; hot coolant can scald.

steps.title: Engine oil level
steps.instruction: Drive at least about 6.2 miles (10 km) without stopping so the engine is at operating temperature. Then use the turn-indicator lever buttons (button 1 until OIL appears, then button 2) or iDrive Vehicle Info > Vehicle status > Engine oil level and wait for the result (about 3 minutes stationary, 5 driving). Add oil only if the display asks, at most 1 US quart (1 L), and within 125 miles. Oil spec and filler: see guide 16.
warnings: Do not overfill; 'level too high' needs a workshop check.
Adding oil to a cold or just-driven reading before the display asks can overfill.

steps.title: Coolant
steps.instruction: With the engine cold, find the translucent expansion tank (reported on the passenger side toward the firewall; the owner's manual shows it as an engine-compartment item, with the diesel tank on the opposite side). Turn the cap slightly counterclockwise to relieve pressure, then open it. The level should be between the MAX and MIN marks in the filler neck. If low, add slowly only BMW-approved coolant mixed 50/50 with distilled water, without overfilling, then close the cap until it clicks. Have repeated loss investigated.
warnings: Repeated low coolant means a leak; do not keep topping up.
Coolant is toxic to pets; clean spills.

steps.title: Brake fluid
steps.instruction: The brake fluid reservoir is on the driver's side at the base of the windshield, under a plastic cover that on E9x cars is the cabin microfilter housing cover (an E92 M3 write-up removes three 8 mm bolts; other sources give four or six, see guide 10). Clean around the reservoir, read the level against the MIN and MAX marks on its side, and if below MIN top up with fresh DOT 4 to just below MAX. Refit the cover.
warnings: A falling level can mean worn pads or a leak; get it inspected.
Brake fluid damages paint; wipe spills at once with water.
Use only sealed, new DOT 4; do not use fluid from an open container.

steps.title: Washer fluid
steps.instruction: Fill the washer reservoir through the engine-bay filler neck (one source: passenger side near the strut tower, black cap with a wiper symbol), which also feeds the headlamp washers. Total system about 6.3 US qt / 6.0 L including headlamp washers; stop about two inches below the cap per one source.
warnings: Use fluid rated for your climate; no BMW additive restriction was found.

steps.title: Power steering (inspection only)
steps.instruction: The owner's manual does not list a power steering reservoir among owner-serviced items, and some cars have electric steering. If your car has a hydraulic reservoir, only look for leaks and a level in the translucent range; topping up (CHF 11S per two parts catalogs) is best left to a shop until the reservoir type is confirmed on the car.
warnings: Do not use ATF or random fluid; wrong fluid damages the pump.

steps.title: Transmission and differential
steps.instruction: Not a routine owner check; out of scope until BMW service data and the car's transmission/drive type are confirmed.

safety: Engine cold before opening the coolant cap; hot coolant can scald.
Brake fluid is corrosive to paint and absorbs moisture; keep containers sealed and use only new fluid.
Low brake fluid or brake system leaks are safety-critical; seek inspection.
Coolant is toxic to pets; clean spills.
Keep wiper arms down when opening the hood (BMW manual) and do not drop fasteners into the cowl.
missingEvidence: BMW owner's-manual text for brake fluid (DOT 4) and its interval for an E9x; the retrievable MY2011 pages mention brake fluid only as a CBS item. MY2010 manual text unreadable.
Washer fluid spec/additives and exact filler position (only one source gives position).
Power steering: confirmation per VIN of hydraulic vs EPS, reservoir location, check procedure and fluid capacity.
Automatic transmission and differential/transfer case fluid info.
Expansion tank location from a second independent source.
Brake reservoir cover fastener count for a 2010 E90 (3, 4 and 6 reported).
Brake fluid capacity; reservoir cap torque.
ownerInputsNeeded: Confirm manual vs automatic and RWD vs xDrive.
Open the hood and note whether a power steering reservoir exists (and whether it is active-steering type).
Photograph the coolant, brake and washer caps so the printed specs/markings can be recorded.
Count the screws on your cabin microfilter housing cover if you will reach the brake reservoir.
Provide the owner's manual fluid/capacity pages if available.

visuals.title: Where the owner-serviceable fluid fill points are in the engine bay

elements.describe: The cap on the translucent coolant expansion tank, with a filler neck marked MAX and MIN; reported on the passenger side toward the firewall.
The washer-fluid filler neck cap, reported black with a wiper symbol, serving window and headlamp washers.
The engine oil filler neck cap on top of the engine.
The brake fluid reservoir at the driver-side base of the windshield, hidden under a long plastic cover.
The base of the windshield and wiper arms for orientation.

facts.note: Manual lists the expansion tank as engine-compartment item; location text not retrievable.
tpautorepair: passenger side near the firewall; youcanic: in the engine compartment in front of the passenger side.
Manual: level between max and min marks in the filler neck. tpautorepair: MIN and MAX on the tank side or a float, black cap. These differ; do not draw detailed marks.
Single source: passenger side near the strut tower, black cap with a wiper symbol. BMW manuals confirm a filler neck exists for headlamp and window washers.
Manual lists the engine oil filler neck; bmwtuning.co says the cap is on top of the engine cover.
Driver side at the base of the windshield under a plastic cover (E92 M3, generic E9x article, E82 thread, generic 3-series article).
Cover is the cabin microfilter housing (E92 M3: remove cabin filter housing bolts; generic article: 'microfilter housing').
bmwtuning: cap right on top of the engine cover; RealOEM lists the cap for oil filler (11128655331) as item 12 of the cylinder head cover diagram, i.e. on the valve cover.
All say a brake reservoir/master cylinder sits driver side at the windshield base beneath a plastic cover (bmwblog on an E92 M3, youcanic on E90-E93, gearshifters generic 3-series).
